chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj and others from one of the Imams (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who reverted from Islam, it was said: He is asked to repent; if he repents, well and good, otherwise he is killed. It was said to Jamil: What do you say if he repents and then reverted from Islam again? He said: He is asked to repent. It was said: What do you say if he repented, then reverted, then repented, then reverted? He said: I have not heard anything specific about this, but in my view, he is like the adulterer upon whom the hadd punishment is carried out twice, and then he is killed thereafter.

key_terms.يُقَامُ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ: The hadd punishment is carried out upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an apostate who repeatedly reverts to Islam and then back to disbelief?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Jamil ibn Darraj elucidates the fiqh of apostasy by drawing a qiyas (analogy) to the punishment for zina, suggesting that repeated apostasy after repentance warrants execution, mirroring the triple-lashing and subsequent death for an adulterer who commits the act multiple times. This view highlights the Shia scholarly approach to determining whether the apostate's repentance is sufficient to reset the legal status or if persistent disbelief necessitates a more severe, cumulative penalty. The narration underscores the procedural emphasis on giving the apostate opportunities to return to Islam before final execution.
